correctness.rationale: The irrational coefficient of (u-lambda sqrt d)^k is -lambda F_{k,d}(u,lambda), so for lambda>0 the rationality conditions are exactly F_{k,d}=1. Over C the degree-(k-1) binary form has simple roots indexed by nontrivial k-th roots of unity via a Mobius ratio, hence the projective plane curve F(U,V)=W^(k-1) is smooth of genus (k-2)(k-3)/2 (including infinity). k=2 forces u=1/2; k=3 is a rational conic with either no rational points or infinitely many and lambda sign normalization; k=4 maps to Y²=X³−4d³ by X=d/u,Y=2d²lambda/u, with Y!=0 so positive-lambda solutions correspond to E_d(Q) nonzero modulo sign. For d=15, P=(60,450), 2P=(24,-18), 5P has nonintegral x=167460/3721; Nagell–Lutz on the integral nonsingular model implies positive rank. For k>=5, g>=3 and Faltings yields finiteness for fixed d,k. Independently computed exact rational 2P and input identity.
